A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QuantSparse. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original QuantSparse video-generation evaluations, component ablations, attention analyses, and computational-resource measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds diagnostic experiments, ablations, and Hunyuan-DiT image-generation results.

M1.justification: MSAD, its loss, and the SSAR/SVD correction procedure are retained. Equation 7 explicitly adds aggregation over attention heads before salient-token selection, whereas v1 omits head indexing. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the implemented selection procedure or clarifies its earlier description. Algorithm 1 otherwise documents the existing pipeline.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix K adds text-to-image generation on DrawBench using Hunyuan-DiT. This extends evaluation beyond the video-generation tasks covered in v1. Existing OpenSORA-prompt and VBench video coverage remains; moving HunyuanVideo results into Table 2 does not add coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 13 adds full-attention distillation as a performance comparator to MSAD; v1 Figure 3 only compared its attention-memory cost. The established quantization and sparsification baseline sets remain. Evaluating QuaRot and Q-VDiT on DrawBench extends their coverage without introducing new baseline methods.

E3.justification: The original 50-step video evaluation and 20-sample, 15-epoch calibration settings remain. Added experiments introduce cache intervals 3–6, attention densities 10–25%, a 1000-sample attention-MSE diagnostic, a full-attention distillation control, and W4A8 evaluation of the 1.5B Hunyuan-DiT. These are targeted protocol extensions.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation of the framework's rationale and design choices: Table 8 isolates quantization, sparsification, and their interaction; Figures 8–9 add four paired attention-error examples; Table 5 tests cache-interval and density trade-offs; Table 13 compares MSAD against full-attention distillation. Existing saliency, SVD, and component ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing temporal singular-value mean/variance plots are retained. The new 1000-sample diagnostic specifies sample size, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Substantial new findings accompany the added experiments. v3 reports attention MSE of 0.685 for combined compression versus 0.216 and 0.134 separately; full-attention distillation and MSAD achieve 15.25 and 15.22 PSNR respectively at substantially different resource costs; DrawBench results give QuantSparse 20.34 PSNR versus Q-VDiT's 19.32. New sensitivity results and baseline latency entries also appear. Matched original video benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 7 revises the written saliency definition from summation over one token index to explicit summation over heads and tokens. The other substantive equations, Propositions 3.1–3.3, Theorem 3.4, and its Appendix A proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about amplified attention shift, MSAD, SSAR, and compression-quality benefits. The headline HunyuanVideo result remains 20.88 PSNR with 3.68× storage compression and 1.88× acceleration.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes occasional improvements over full precision to emphasizing task-critical tokens, suppressing irrelevant attention, and stabilizing temporal behavior. New discussion explains cache-interval and density choices and interprets DrawBench results as evidence of applicability to image generation. No substantive new limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v3 adds calibration-to-inference pseudocode and specifies A800 80GB hardware, CUDA 12.4, and CUTLASS integer matrix multiplication through PyTorch. Table 13 also documents attention-map dimensions. Existing calibration hyperparameters remain, and both versions still describe the same code repository as forthcoming.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including S2Q-VDiT, MPQ-DMv2, AffineQuant, Hunyuan-DiT, DrawBench's source work, and CUTLASS, while removing the Krishnamoorthi whitepaper reference. The central positioning around combining quantization and sparsification remains. Q-VDiT's publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: a new overall-pipeline subsection, expanded experimental explanations, an image-generation appendix, acknowledgements, affiliation updates, and some terminology corrections. Appendix H reorders existing discussions. Most of the original narrative and section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially restructured to combine both large video models with quality and latency columns, incorporating existing appendix results. v3 also adds four experimental tables, paired attention-map figures, and an algorithm display, and reformats the SVD ablation table. Existing video examples and earlier analytical figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for the existing framework through direct compression-interaction measurements, full-attention distillation comparisons, and cache/density sensitivity tests. Image-generation results and clearer implementation documentation add useful breadth and reproducibility. These are targeted gains to an already extensively evaluated paper; the main results and proof remain unchanged, and the new explanation for outperforming full precision is not directly isolated experimentally.
